findings.title: Restore projection files after partial writes
findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
findings.originalBody:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore projection files after partial writes**

If an I/O error occurs after `open('wb')` truncates an overwritten file, or after `open('xb')` creates a new file, this path is already in `synchronized_paths`, but restoration later accepts only the complete postimage or original baseline and therefore preserves the runner's partial output as if it were concurrent drift. The replay's interrupted-write fixture throws before truncation, so it does not cover this case; a disk or external-volume write failure can consequently leave the projection short of its required restored 1,008 inputs. Use an atomic temporary-file replacement or otherwise distinguish and restore runner-created partial writes from foreign changes.

findings.title: Keep discovery decisions on the supplied process snapshot
findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
findings.originalBody:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep discovery decisions on the supplied process snapshot**

When `details(pid)` fails during descendant discovery, this fallback calls `ps()` again and decides whether to reject the child from that different snapshot. A child exit or PID turnover between the two queries therefore makes the claimed same-snapshot identity result unprovable; the offline assertion misses this because it checks for direct `ps()` calls only in `monitor` and `snapshot_consumers`, not in `discover`. Fail the supplied-snapshot cycle deterministically instead of querying another process population.
